_about: KIKO's curated learning content. Facts here are checked by people, so KIKO never invents them. Add items freely: the Playroom and the server read this file on start. Animals may have a "speak" field: how KIKO says the sound out loud when the written sound isn't easy to read (like "Grrr!").

stories.title: The Thirsty Crow
lines: It was a hot, hot day.
A crow was very thirsty.
He looked and looked for water.
At last, he found a pot with a little water at the bottom.
His beak could not reach it!
The crow had an idea.
He dropped small stones into the pot, one by one.
Plop, plop, plop! The water came up and up.
Now the crow could drink. Ahh!
stories.lesson: When we think, we can solve a problem.

stories.title: The Monkey and the Crocodile
lines: A monkey lived in a jamun tree by the river.
He shared sweet jamun fruits with his friend, the crocodile.
One day the crocodile said, "Come for a ride on my back!"
In the middle of the river, the crocodile said, "My wife wants to eat your heart!"
The monkey thought fast.
"Oh no! I left my heart up in the tree," he said. "Let's go back and get it."
The crocodile swam back to the tree.
Hop! The monkey jumped up into his tree, safe and sound.
"A heart stays inside you, silly!" he called.
stories.lesson: Stay calm and think, even when you feel scared.

stories.title: The Lion and the Mouse
lines: A big lion was sleeping under a tree.
A tiny mouse ran over his nose. The lion woke up!
"Please let me go," squeaked the mouse. "One day I will help you."
The lion laughed. "How can a tiny mouse help me?" But he let the mouse go.
A few days later, the lion got stuck in a big net.
He could not get out.
The little mouse came running.
Nibble, nibble, nibble! She chewed the net open.
The lion was free! "Thank you, little friend," he said.
stories.lesson: Even a small friend can be a big help.

stories.title: Tenali Raman and the Thieves
lines: Tenali Raman was a clever man in the king's court.
One night, he saw thieves hiding near his house.
Tenali spoke loudly to his wife so the thieves could hear.
"Let's hide our gold box in the well!"
He dropped a heavy box of stones into the well. Splash!
All night, the thieves pulled up water from the well to find the box.
The water ran into Tenali's garden.
By morning, all his plants had a big drink!
The tired thieves found only stones, and they ran away.
stories.lesson: A clever idea can fix a problem without any fighting.

stories.title: Birbal Counts the Crows
lines: One day, King Akbar asked a tricky question.
"Birbal, how many crows are there in our city?"
Birbal smiled and thought for a moment.
"There are ninety-five thousand, four hundred and sixty-three crows," he said.
"What if there are fewer?" asked the king.
"Then some crows went to visit their friends in other towns!"
"And what if there are more?"
"Then some crow friends came to visit us!"
King Akbar laughed and laughed.
stories.lesson: A happy, quick mind can answer tricky questions.

stories.title: The Hare and the Tortoise
lines: A hare liked to boast. "I am the fastest!" he said.
A slow tortoise said, "Let's have a race."
The hare laughed, and the race began.
Zoom! The hare ran far ahead.
"The tortoise is so slow. I will take a nap," he said.
The tortoise kept walking, step by step.
He did not stop. Step, step, step.
The hare woke up and ran fast, but it was too late.
The tortoise had already won the race!
stories.lesson: Slow and steady wins the race.

stories.title: The Ant and the Dove
lines: A little ant went to the river for a drink.
Oops! She fell into the water.
A kind dove saw her and dropped a leaf.
The ant climbed onto the leaf and floated safely to the shore.
Later, a hunter came with a net to catch the dove.
The ant saw him. She gave his foot a quick little pinch!
"Ouch!" said the hunter, and he dropped his net.
The dove flew away, safe and free.
The two friends were very happy.
stories.lesson: When you are kind, kindness comes back to you.

stories.title: The Little Shy Star
lines: High in the night sky lived a little star named Tara.
Tara was shy. She hid behind a soft cloud.
Down below, a little boy could not sleep.
"I wish I could see a star," he whispered.
Tara heard him. She took a deep breath.
Slowly, she peeked out from the cloud and twinkled.
The boy smiled a big, sleepy smile.
"Goodnight, little star," he said, and closed his eyes.
Tara twinkled softly all night long.
stories.lesson: A little bit of brave can make someone happy.

happy.say: Yay! I love that you feel happy. What made you smile today?

sad.say: It's okay to feel sad. Let's take a slow breath together. A hug from a grown-up you love can help too.

angry.say: Angry feelings are big. Let's squeeze our hands tight, then let go. Breathe out slowly, like blowing a candle.

scared.say: You are safe with me. Tell a grown-up you trust what scared you. They can help.

tired.say: Your body wants some rest. A cozy story and a little sleep will help.

play_ideas: Let's play I Spy! Look around and find something red.
Build the tallest tower you can with blocks or cups.
Draw your favourite animal, then make its sound!
Dance like a peacock until the music in your head stops.
Make a paper boat with a grown-up and float it in a tub of water.
Hop like a frog five times, then stretch like a tall tree.
